title: Fwd Cargo Door Surround Fitting — Corner Crack Stop Drill and Reinforcing Angle

ata.title: Fuselage Section 13 — Forward — Door Surround Structure

abstract: Interim repair for cracking at the lower corner of the forward cargo door surround fitting, using a stop drill and a bolted reinforcing angle, valid only until the fitting can be replaced.

sections.purpose: This repair arrests a crack at the lower corner of the forward cargo door surround fitting and restores enough static capability for continued operation until the fitting is replaced at the next opportunity.
sections.damage_assessment: Find the crack tip by dye penetrant inspection and mark it. Cracks up to 18 mm in length, originating at the corner radius and not crossing a fastener row, are inside this repair. A crack that has reached a fastener hole, that has branched, or that lies in the frame sub-assembly rather than in the fitting, is outside it and requires an engineering assessment. Measure the crack length from the radius tangent point, not from the visible surface break, because the subsurface extent is typically 3 to 5 mm longer. Do an eddy current inspection of the opposite corner of the same fitting before deciding on the repair; symmetrical cracking usually means the load path has changed and a single-corner repair will not hold.
sections.repair_procedure: Stop drill the crack 4 mm beyond the marked tip with a 4.8 mm drill, and ream the hole to remove the drilled surface. Do a dye penetrant inspection of the stop drill hole to confirm the crack tip is contained. Cut the reinforcing angle from the fitting kit D5321131361369 material to the layout of repair drawing RD-53-21-13-003 and drill the fastener pattern using the angle as a template. The inboard row is set out 12 mm from the sealant land at the frame foot, which is the datum for every dimension on sheet 2. Do not drill into the frame sub-assembly D5321134517524; the drawing gives the exclusion boundary. Apply the chromate-free primer to all new surfaces. Install the angle wet with sealant and fasten it with washers AES963502K7 and plain washers AGS46790-6A at the pitch on the drawing. Fit silicone edging grommets where the angle crosses a systems penetration. Restore the continuous sealant bead along the frame foot after the angle is installed.
sections.inspection_requirements: This repair is interim and is limited to 6 000 flight cycles or twenty-four months from embodiment, whichever occurs first, after which the fitting must be replaced. Do a repeat dye penetrant inspection of the stop drill hole and of the angle perimeter every 1 500 flight cycles. Any growth from the stop drill hole makes the repair invalid immediately. Record the repair against the aircraft and notify Aeralis within ten days.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Cracks up to 18 mm measured from the radius tangent point, originating at the corner radius, not crossing a fastener row and not branched. One crack per fitting.

repair_drawings.title: Stop drill and reinforcing angle, fwd cargo door surround fitting

type_data.fastener_pattern: Two rows of 18 fasteners at 18 mm pitch and 12 mm edge distance measured from the sealant land, staggered, with the exclusion boundary on sheet 2 left unfastened
type_data.fatigue_life_note: Interim repair limited to 6 000 flight cycles or twenty-four months; repeat dye penetrant inspection every 1 500 flight cycles.

issue.reason: The inboard row edge distance is made dependent on the protection standard and a sealing land note is added so that the interrupted land is not closed by the repair.

ata.title: Fuselage Section 13 — Forward — Door Surround Structure

abstract: Interim repair for cracking at the lower corner of the forward cargo door surround fitting, using a stop drill and a bolted reinforcing angle, valid only until the fitting can be replaced.

Cut the reinforcing angle from the fitting kit D5321131361369 material to the layout of repair drawing RD-53-21-13-003 and drill the fastener pattern using the angle as a template. Establish the protection standard of the surround before the template is positioned. Fit silicone edging grommets where the angle crosses a systems penetration. Restore the sealing at the frame foot, keeping the interrupted land clear on aircraft that have it. The angle must not bridge the interruption; where the layout would close it, mask the land and leave the angle short.
sections.inspection_requirements: This repair is interim and is limited to 6 000 flight cycles or twenty-four months from embodiment, whichever occurs first, after which the fitting must be replaced. Do a repeat dye penetrant inspection of the stop drill hole and of the angle perimeter every 1 500 flight cycles. Any growth from the stop drill hole makes the repair invalid immediately. Record the repair against the aircraft and notify Aeralis within ten days.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Cracks up to 18 mm measured from the radius tangent point, originating at the corner radius, not crossing a fastener row and not branched. One crack per fitting.

type_data.fastener_pattern: Two rows of 18 fasteners at 18 mm pitch, staggered. Inboard row edge distance is 12 mm from the sealant land on the original protection standard and 16 mm on the chromate-free standard; the exclusion boundary on sheet 2 is left unfastened
type_data.fatigue_life_note: Interim repair limited to 6 000 flight cycles or twenty-four months; repeat dye penetrant inspection every 1 500 flight cycles.
